title_en: Shenzhen Yizhifan Trade Co., Ltd. and Hou Qingbin v. Shenzhen Zhaobangji Group Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Kangnuofu Information Consulting Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd., and Third Party Guangdong Lizhao Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: 1. The establishment of a transfer guarantee shall occur before the maturity of the debt performance period. However, regarding the realization of the transfer guarantee, with reference to Article 170 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, conditions such as the debtor's failure to perform the due debt or the occurrence of circumstances agreed by the parties for realizing the right must be satisfied. Where the parties agree in the contract establishing the transfer guarantee that if the value of the collateral is insufficient to cover the relevant debt, the creditor is entitled to claim the exercise of the transfer guarantee right even before the debt performance period has expired. Such an agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations and shall be deemed lawful and valid.

full_text_en:
Shenzhen Yizhifan Trading Co., Ltd. and Hou Qingbin v. Shenzhen Zhaobangji Group Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Kangnuofu Information Consulting Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd., and Third Party Guangdong Lizhao Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over contract

【Ruling Summary】

1. A surrender-based guarantee should be established before the expiration of the debt performance period. However, regarding the realization of such a guarantee, by reference to Article 170 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, the conditions for realization include the debtor's failure to perform the matured debt or the occurrence of circumstances agreed by the parties for realizing the rights. Where the parties agree in the contract establishing the surrender-based guarantee that, if the value of the secured property is insufficient to cover the relevant debt, the creditor is entitled to claim exercise of the rights under the surrender-based guarantee even before the debt performance period has expired, such an agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations and shall be deemed lawful and valid.

2. To prevent circumstances similar to fluid pledges or fluid mortgages, where the creditor obtains the value of the subject matter exceeding the amount of the debt, the realization of the rights under a surrender-based guarantee shall impose a liquidation obligation on the parties. The consensus reached by the parties on the value of the subject matter of the surrender-based guarantee may be recognized as an effective method of determining the value of the subject matter. Where the value of the subject matter of the surrender-based guarantee has already been determined, but both parties foresee that the amount of the debt may change, the parties shall still perform the corresponding liquidation obligation on the basis of the final settled debt amount.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2018) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 751

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shenzhen Yizhifan Trading Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 308, 3rd Floor, #1 Science and Technology Building, Xinno Building, No. 433 Dongbin Road, Nanshan District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Luo Xiaotang, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zeng Chenhua, lawyer of Guangdong Baoyuan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ma Jie, lawyer of Beijing Junzejun Law Firm.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hou Qingbin, male, born on October 12, 1954, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Yingze District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xiaohua, lawyer of Shanxi Bangning Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xujuan, lawyer of Shanxi Bangning Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Zhaobangji Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floor P, Atrium, Department Store Square Building, No. 123 Shennan East Road, Dongmen Street, Luohu District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Fusheng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yaoquan, lawyer of Beijing Tiantong (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ji Shuxiong, lawyer of Beijing Deheng (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Kangnuofu Information Consulting Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1201, 12th Floor, Zhaobangji Building, southwest corner of the intersection of Caitian Road and Fuhua Road, Futian Street, Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yu, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Qian, lawyer of Beijing Tiantong (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Guo Chunnuan, lawyer of Beijing Deheng (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floor P, Atrium, Department Store Square Building, No. 123 Shennan East Road, Dongmen Street, Luohu District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Fusheng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lin Taisong, lawyer of Guoxin Xinyang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ma Biao, lawyer of Guoxin Xinyang Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Guangdong Lizhao Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled in Ailinggen Yueshan Village, Dalingshan Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Hu Liming, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Guan Yiqiao, lawyer of Shanxi Bangning Law Firm.

The appellants, Shenzhen Yizhifan Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yizhifan Company) and Hou Qingbin, appealed against the civil judgment (2016) Yue First Civil No. 52 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the case of a dispute over contract with the appellees, Shenzhen Zhaobangji Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhaobangji Company), Shenzhen Kangnuofu Information Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kangnuofu Company), and Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Liyumen Company), and the third party at first instance Guangdong Lizhao Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lizhao Company), respectively filing appeals to this Court. After accepting the case on July 19, 2018, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. The agents ad litem of appellant Yizhifan Company, Zeng Chenhua and Ma Jie, the appellant Hou Qingbin and his agents ad litem Wang Xiaohua and Zhang Xujuan, the agents ad litem of appellee Zhaobangji Company, Chen Yaoquan and Ji Shuxiong, the agents ad litem of appellee Kangnuofu Company, Li Qian and Guo Chunnuan, the agents ad litem of appellee Liyumen Company, Lin Taisong and Ma Biao, and the agent ad litem of third party at first instance Lizhao Company, Guan Yiqiao, appeared in court. This case has now been concluded.

On May 26, 2014, Shenzhen Anlian Xinno Investment Development Co., Ltd. changed its name to Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd. On February 13, 2018, Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd. changed its name to Shenzhen Liqiao Investment Development Co., Ltd. On June 6, 2018, Shenzhen Liqiao Investment Development Co., Ltd. changed its name back to Shenzhen Liyumen Investment Development Co., Ltd. Shenzhen Anlian Xinno Investment Development Co., Ltd. and Shenzhen Liqiao Investment Development Co., Ltd. are hereinafter uniformly referred to as Liyumen Company. On March 21, 2018, Shenzhen Kangnuofu Investment Development Co., Ltd. changed its name to Shenzhen Kangnuofu Information Consulting Co., Ltd., which is hereinafter uniformly referred to as Kangnuofu Company.

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin appealed requesting: to set aside the first instance judgment and instead rule in favor of all claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin in the first instance; and to order Zhaobangji Company, Kangnuofu Company, and Liyumen Company to bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances. Facts and Reasons: 1. The "Project Cooperation Agreement" signed by all parties on April 2, 2014 (hereinafter referred to as the 4.2 "Project Cooperation Agreement"), the "Equity Guarantee Agreement" signed on April 25, 2014 (hereinafter referred to as the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement"), the "Agreement" signed on August 26, 2014 (hereinafter referred to as the 8.26 "Agreement"), and the "Supplemental Agreement to the August 26, 2014 <Agreement> of the Four Parties" signed on November 17, 2015 (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplemental Agreement") actually constitute a series of overall agreements concerning a "surrender-based guarantee" of 30% equity, which are consistent, indivisible, and have not been terminated or altered in any way. According to consistent practice in judicial practice, a surrender-based guarantee does not have the effect of transferring property rights. The court should first confirm that Yizhifan Company enjoys the 30% equity in Liyumen Company and the corresponding project rights and interests. 2. The 8.26 "Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" are not equity transfer agreements, and they violate the mandatory liquidation obligation of the surrender-based guarantee and the principle of fairness and equivalent compensation. By reference to the prohibition on fluid pledges, they should be confirmed as null and void in accordance with the law. First, the 8.26 "Agreement" at issue has always emphasized the continued performance of the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement". In substance, the "Agreement" requires Yizhifan Company to "forcibly relinquish the security property" when the "debt has not yet fallen due and without liquidation". This agreement contains no expression of intent to "terminate the guarantee" or to "transfer the equity". The first instance judgment, while finding that the stipulation on 30% equity in the 4.2 "Project Cooperation Agreement" and the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" constituted a surrender-based guarantee, and without any supporting basis, determined that the 8.26 "Agreement" terminated the original surrender-based guarantee and transformed it into an equity transfer, which is clearly erroneous. Second, when the 8.26 "Agreement" was signed, Yizhifan Company's external debts had not yet fallen due, and there was no issue of Yizhifan Company being unable to repay them, necessitating repayment by Zhaobangji Company on its behalf. At the same time, when the 8.26 "Agreement" was signed, the 30% equity was not appraised as provided in the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement". Since the value of the "security property" and the amount of the "secured debt" were both undetermined, the conditions for liquidation were not met, and in fact no liquidation was carried out. Although this case does not fall directly within the scope of regulation by Article 211 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, it should still comply with the basic principles of civil law such as fairness and equivalent compensation embodied in that legal provision. Accordingly, Zhaobangji Company, taking advantage of its superior bargaining position as a creditor, forcibly demanded that Yizhifan Company relinquish the 30% equity to offset its external debts of RMB 406,000,000. The 8.26 "Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" signed in this manner should be confirmed as null and void in accordance with the law. 3. The conditions for rescission of the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" under both agreement and law are satisfied, and the industrial and commercial registration of Yizhifan Company's 30% equity should be restored. First, the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" meets the conditions for agreed rescission. The agreement stipulated that, without Yizhifan Company's consent, the 30% equity may not be pledged; otherwise, Yizhifan Company has the right to demand the return of that portion of the equity. However, according to the facts found by the first instance court, Kangnuofu Company and Zhaobangji Company had already pledged the equity they held to the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Shenzhen Hongwei Sub-branch and the Agricultural Bank of China Shenzhen Overseas Chinese Town Sub-branch respectively on April 8, 2015. Since this pledge was made without Yizhifan Company's consent, under the contract, Yizhifan Company is entitled to request the restoration of the registration change for the 30% equity. Second, the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" also meets the conditions for statutory rescission. The core contractual purpose of the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" includes two aspects: first, the 30% equity still belongs to Yizhifan Company; second, Yizhifan Company will liquidate the value of the 30% equity and related rights against its payable debts and obtain proceeds. However, after the agreement was signed, the following actions taken by Zhaobangji Company made the above contractual purposes impossible to achieve: First, on August 26, 2014, only four months after the signing of the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement", and when the debt had not yet matured, the amount of the debt was undetermined, no appraisal of the 30% equity as security and its market value had been conducted, and no liquidation between the amount of the debt and the value of the security property had been performed, Zhaobangji Company disposed of the 30% equity and corresponding project rights enjoyed by Yizhifan Company, completely frustrating the contractual purpose. Second, on April 2, 2015, Liyumen Company, as borrower and mortgagor, entered into a "Maximum Mortgage Contract" with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Shenzhen Hongwei Sub-branch and the Agricultural Bank of China Shenzhen Overseas Chinese Town Sub-branch, mortgaging all of its land to secure a principal debt of RMB 1,248,789,960. Liyumen Company is a project company whose core assets are only the land use right and the project under construction. Liyumen Company mortgaged its core assets externally, with the amount as high as RMB 1.248 billion, thereby seriously impairing Yizhifan Company's 30% project rights, making it impossible to achieve the contractual purpose of liquidating the 30% equity under the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement". Given the above illegal disposal of the 30% equity by Zhaobangji Company and the external mortgage of the land under Liyumen Company's name, which seriously damaged Yizhifan Company's core interests in enjoying the 30% equity and settling the 30% equity in accordance with the agreement under the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement", rendering the contractual purpose unattainable, the contract should be rescinded. In summary, Yizhifan Company used its 30% equity in Liyumen Company to create a security by entering into three sets of agreements, namely the 4.2 "Project Cooperation Agreement", the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement", the 8.26 "Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement". In each of these agreements, the expression of intent regarding the surrender-based guarantee is consistent and has never been terminated. The 8.26 "Agreement", which stipulates that Yizhifan Company relinquishes the security property when the debt has not yet matured and without liquidation, clearly violates the mandatory liquidation obligation of the surrender-based guarantee and the principles of fairness and equivalent compensation. The first instance judgment's determination that the 8.26 "Agreement" is an equity transfer agreement clearly contradicts the evidence and objective facts of this case and misapplies the law. Please amend the judgment in accordance with the law.

Zhaobangji Company, Kangnuofu Company, and Liyumen Company argued in defense: 1. After Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin transferred the 30% equity in Liyumen Company to Zhaobangji Company for RMB 406,000,000, they had previously filed multiple lawsuits and later withdrew them. Now they bring this lawsuit again in bad faith, seeking the return of the already transferred equity, which clearly violates commercial good faith. Their true purpose is to use litigation to extort property from Zhaobangji Company. 2. The nature of the 8.26 "Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" involved in this case is an equity transfer agreement. The transfer of the 30% equity and its rights and interests was the true expression of intent of all parties and did not violate the mandatory provisions of the law. The transfer of the 30% equity at issue is lawful and valid, and the first instance court's determination in this regard is correct. 3. The provisions of the 4.2 "Project Cooperation Agreement" and the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" do not constitute a surrender-based guarantee, and the 8.26 "Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" also do not constitute a fluid guarantee contract as claimed by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin. First, Zhaobangji Company is not the creditor of the specific debts listed in the agreements that Yizhifan Company should repay, and Zhaobangji Company has no underlying principal debt basis for entering into a guarantee agreement with Yizhifan Company. Second, in the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement", Yizhifan Company did not completely transfer the 30% equity at issue to Zhaobangji Company, but placed it under joint management by both parties, which does not meet the characteristics of a surrender-based guarantee and does not constitute a surrender-based guarantee. The guarantee function arising from the joint equity management formed by the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" was terminated by the subsequent 8.26 "Agreement". Third, Zhaobangji Company acquired the 30% equity at issue for a clear and fixed consideration of RMB 406,000,000, and agreed with Yizhifan Company to repay its external debts within the scope of RMB 406,000,000. If the amount was insufficient, Yizhifan Company remained responsible for repayment; if there was a surplus, it would be paid to the payee designated by Yizhifan Company, rather than directly using the 30% equity at issue to offset the debts Yizhifan Company should repay. Finally, the "Supplemental Agreement" confirmed the actual performance of the 8.26 "Agreement". This "Supplemental Agreement", formed one year, three months, and fifteen days later, further confirms that the true expression of intent of the parties in the 8.26 "Agreement" was to transfer the 30% equity at issue, and not a fluid contract. 4. The "Supplemental Grounds for Appeal" submitted by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin depart from their claims and vigorously deny the validity of the transfer of 70% equity in an attempt to confuse the objective facts. The issue of the validity of the transfer of 70% equity is not within the scope of adjudication of this case. In summary, the appellate claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin are all baseless in law and should be dismissed by the court of second instance.

Lizhao Company stated: 1. It accepts the first instance court's finding that the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" is a surrender-based guarantee in nature, but does not accept that the 8.26 "Agreement" and other supplemental agreements terminated the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement". The 8.26 "Agreement" is a continuation of performance of the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement" and does not constitute a renewed disposition of the equity. 2. It does not accept the "Appraisal Report" submitted by Yizhifan Company. The report's appraisal method is incorrect, as it fails to consider that the project enjoyed preferential treatment under the Shenzhen Urban Renewal Measures and that the land is commercial rather than industrial. The "Appraisal Report" also does not reflect Liyumen Company's liabilities, and the financial data is inaccurate and of no reference value.

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin filed the following claims with the first instance court: 1. Request a judgment to confirm that the 8.26 "Agreement" and the "Supplemental Agreement" are null and void; 2. Request a judgment to rescind the 4.25 "Equity Guarantee Agreement"; 3. Request a judgment ordering Zhaobangji Company and Kangnuofu Company to jointly return to Yizhifan Company the 30% equity in Liyumen Company held by them and to complete the procedures for industrial and commercial registration; 4. Request a judgment confirming that Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin enjoy 30% of the project rights and interests of Liyumen Company (the 30% equity in Liyumen Company and the corresponding project rights and interests corresponding to the above claims 1, 2, 3, and 4 are currently appraised at RMB 705,043,400); 5. Request that all litigation costs of this case be borne by Zhaobangji Company, Kangnuofu Company, and Liyumen Company.

The court of first instance found the following upon trial:

I. Signing and Performance of the 4.2 "Project Cooperation Agreement"

On April 2, 2014, Yizhifan Company, Zhaobangji Company, Hou Qingbin, and Lizhao Company entered into a Project Cooperation Agreement. The agreement confirmed that Yizhifan Company held 100% equity of Liyumen Company, Hou Qingbin was the actual controller of Liyumen Company, and Lizhao Company, as an affiliate of Hou Qingbin, assumed guarantee liability jointly with Hou Qingbin. The agreement stipulated that Yizhifan Company would transfer 70% equity of Liyumen Company to Zhaobangji Company, with the equity transfer price at RMB 7 million and the investment compensation at RMB 938 million, to cover Liyumen Company's liabilities. At the same time, Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin disclosed the debts and risks of Liyumen Company. The content regarding the 30% equity in dispute under this agreement was as follows: 1. Yizhifan Company, Hou Qingbin, and Lizhao Company undertook to handle and assume responsibility for the Heijian lawsuit, ensuring that within 20 days after the registration of the transfer of 70% equity of Liyumen Company to Zhaobangji Company, the land seizure would be resolved through replacement or other means. Yizhifan Company undertook to use its 30% equity in Liyumen Company and corresponding undistributed rights and interests as a guarantee for the performance of the above obligations. If Yizhifan Company, Hou Qingbin, and Lizhao Company failed to resolve the matter within one month after the signing of this agreement, Zhaobangji Company had the right to resolve it in its own name or in the name of Liyumen Company; the related costs and expenses incurred would be jointly and severally repaid by Yizhifan Company, Hou Qingbin, and Lizhao Company to Zhaobangji Company, or compensated by Yizhifan Company's equity in Liyumen Company and corresponding undistributed rights and interests. However, when paying such costs or expenses, Zhaobangji Company should negotiate with Yizhifan Company to determine the amount. 2. After Zhaobangji Company became a shareholder of Liyumen Company, if Yizhifan Company lacked funds, Zhaobangji Company was willing to provide financing loans to Yizhifan Company, provided that Yizhifan Company must transfer its 30% equity in Liyumen Company to a company or individual designated by Zhaobangji Company as collateral, with the financing loan amount at RMB 250 million, an annual interest rate of 30%, and repayment within six months after the project's completion and acceptance. Interest was payable annually; if Yizhifan Company failed to pay interest on time, interest on the overdue interest would accrue at an annual rate of 20%. After Yizhifan Company repaid the principal and interest of the loan from Zhaobangji Company, Zhaobangji Company would transfer the 30% equity back to Yizhifan Company. If, after Zhaobangji Company provided financing to Yizhifan Company, Yizhifan Company failed to repay the principal and interest within the agreed time, Yizhifan Company agreed to compensate with its equity in Liyumen Company and corresponding rights and interests, and would unconditionally cooperate with Zhaobangji Company in handling the related compensation procedures. For the above RMB 250 million financing loan, Zhaobangji Company should, within five days after the registration of the transfer of 70% equity of Liyumen Company to Zhaobangji Company, first provide a financing loan of RMB 150 million to Yizhifan Company, specifically for removing the seizure on the target project land and for handling related matters by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin (provided that Yizhifan Company first transferred its 30% equity in Liyumen Company to a company or individual designated by Zhaobangji Company as agreed).

On April 21, 2014, Yizhifan Company registered the transfer of 70% equity of Liyumen Company to Zhaobangji Company.

B. Conclusion and Performance of the April 25 Equity Guarantee Agreement

On April 25, 2014, Yizhifan Company, Zhaobangji Company, and Kangnuofu Company entered into an Equity Guarantee Agreement. The agreement confirmed: 1. To ensure that Yizhifan Company could fulfill its debt repayment and subsequent fund payment obligations, Yizhifan Company was willing to mortgage its 30% equity in Liyumen Company to Kangnuofu Company by way of transfer. The sole shareholder of Kangnuofu Company was currently appointed solely by Zhaobangji Company. Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company decided to change Kangnuofu Company's shareholder structure to a two-person limited company, with Zhaobangji Company holding 51% equity and Luo Xiaotang, appointed by Yizhifan Company, holding 49% equity. 2. The actual owner of the above 30% equity remained Yizhifan Company, which continued to enjoy, exercise, and bear the shareholder rights and obligations corresponding to that 30% equity in the project company. The agreement confirmed that the 30% equity guaranteed the following: (1) resolution of the Heijian lawsuit and seizure; (2) debts incurred by Liyumen Company before Zhaobangji Company became a shareholder and debts not yet discovered; (3) Zhaobangji Company's agreement to provide loans to Yizhifan Company not exceeding RMB 250 million, the loan amount to be calculated based on the actual funds received and confirmed by Yizhifan Company; (4) Liyumen Company had borrowed RMB 310 million from Guangzhou Bank, and would apply for subsequent loans from banks; Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company should repay the loan principal and interest in proportion to their equity; (5) Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company should contribute subsequent development and construction funds for the target project in proportion to their equity. For the above RMB 250 million loan, the agreement stipulated that if Yizhifan Company needed financing loans from Zhaobangji Company, Yizhifan Company should transfer the 49% equity of Kangnuofu Company held by its appointed personnel to Zhaobangji Company or a company (or individual) designated by Zhaobangji Company, as collateral for the financing loan. The agreement set out the following debt settlement: when Liyumen Company completed full completion acceptance, initial registration, and met the conditions for separate property rights registration, the parties would conduct a final settlement of Yizhifan Company's various repayment and payment obligations. After settlement, if Yizhifan Company fully performed its repayment and payment obligations, Yizhifan Company could request the return of the 30% equity; if Yizhifan Company failed to perform or if Zhaobangji Company performed on its behalf, Zhaobangji Company could demand compensation using the rights and interests corresponding to Yizhifan Company's 30% equity in Liyumen Company (i.e., the real estate properties distributable according to the equity ratio), with the specific compensation method being 90% of the assessed market sales price. The liability for breach of contract agreed in the agreement was: during the period when Kangnuofu Company held the 30% equity of the project company transferred by Yizhifan Company as collateral, if Kangnuofu Company, without the consent of Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company, mortgaged, guaranteed, or transferred the 30% equity, Yizhifan Company had the right to request Kangnuofu Company to transfer the 30% equity of the project company to Yizhifan Company; if Kangnuofu Company could not perform, Yizhifan Company had the right to request Zhaobangji Company to transfer the 30% equity of the project company held by it to Yizhifan Company.

On April 23, 2014, Kangnuofu Company's shareholder structure changed from Chen Qiuqiu holding 100% equity to Luo Xiaotang holding 49% equity and Zhaobangji Company holding 51% equity. On April 25, 2014, Yizhifan Company registered the transfer of its 30% equity in Liyumen Company to Kangnuofu Company.

C. Conclusion and Performance of the August 26 Agreement and Supplementary Agreement

On August 26, 2014, Yizhifan Company, Zhaobangji Company, Hou Qingbin, Lizhao Company, and Liyumen Company jointly entered into an Agreement. The recitals of the agreement clarified: 2. On April 25, 2014, Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company, together with Kangnuofu Company, entered into an Equity Guarantee Agreement, which mainly stipulated: (1) To ensure that Yizhifan Company could clean up and repay the debts of Liyumen Company incurred before Zhaobangji Company acquired 70% equity, and to ensure that Zhaobangji Company and the restructured Liyumen Company would not suffer losses, Yizhifan Company agreed to transfer its remaining 30% equity in Liyumen Company to Kangnuofu Company as collateral; (2) If Yizhifan Company could clean up and repay the above debts as agreed (including lifting the seizure on the project land in the Gao Yingcan lawsuit, complete resolution of the entire case, handling of RMB 46 million from Shanxi Jianbang Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jianbang Company), the principal and interest of RMB 310 million loan from Guangzhou Bank attributable to Yizhifan Company, and RMB 80 million overdue interest from Chaoshang Company, etc.), and could invest subsequent construction funds in proportion to its equity, then Yizhifan Company could request Kangnuofu Company to return the 30% equity and enjoy corresponding rights in proportion to its equity. If Yizhifan Company could not repay the debts or could not invest subsequent construction funds in proportion to its equity, after Zhaobangji Company repaid and paid on its behalf, Zhaobangji Company had the right to offset using the rights and interests corresponding to the 30% equity; (3) Considering changes in the real estate market, the parties agreed to entrust a professional appraisal agency annually to assess the rights and interests corresponding to Yizhifan Company's 30% equity to determine whether Yizhifan Company's 30% equity share was sufficient to repay its debts. 3. On May 27, 2014, Yizhifan Company borrowed RMB 50 million from Xu Weishan, an affiliate of Zhaobangji Company, through Zhaobangji Company. Hou Qingbin was the joint and several guarantor for this loan. 4. Due to reasons attributable to Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin, the debts that Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin had clearly failed to clean up and repay as agreed were as follows: (1) lifting the seizure on the project land in the Gao Yingcan lawsuit and complete resolution of the entire case; (2) accounting treatment of RMB 46 million paid by Jianbang Company to Liyumen Company; (3) the remaining RMB 80 million debt arising from loans from Chaoshang Company and its affiliate Wu Yiqun. 5. The debts of Yizhifan Company that had been disclosed but were not yet due were as follows: (1) a loan of RMB 310 million from Guangzhou Bank secured by the project land, with Yizhifan Company liable to repay RMB 93 million in principal and interest according to its equity ratio; (2) Yizhifan Company's obligation to repay the principal and interest of RMB 50 million borrowed from Xu Weishan. 6. After a market assessment of the entire project, Yizhifan Company's equity interest in Liyumen Company was insufficient to repay the above debts. The agreement stipulated: 1. From the effective date of this contract, Yizhifan Company abandoned the 30% equity of Liyumen Company that had been transferred to Kangnuofu Company. The 30% equity belonged to Zhaobangji Company and would be disposed of at Zhaobangji Company's sole discretion. 2. From the effective date of this contract, Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin completely withdrew from Liyumen Company and completely withdrew from the project involved. Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin no longer had any rights in Liyumen Company or the project. 3. From the effective date of this contract, the debts owed by Yizhifan Company, Hou Qingbin, and Lizhao Company as described above would be resolved by Zhaobangji Company and Liyumen Company within the total amount of RMB 406 million. 4. The parties confirmed that the specific allocation of RMB 406 million was as follows: (1) RMB 120 million for the complete resolution of the Gao Yingcan case and lifting of the seizure on the project land. (2) RMB 50 million for handling the RMB 46 million accounts of Jianbang Company. (3) RMB 80 million for settling the remaining RMB 80 million debt arising from loans from Chaoshang Company and its affiliate Wu Yiqun. (4) RMB 100 million for repaying the principal and interest of the Guangzhou Bank loan attributable to Yizhifan Company. (5) RMB 56 million for repaying the principal and interest of the RMB 50 million loan from Xu Weishan. 5. The above five debts would be settled directly by Zhaobangji Company or Liyumen Company with the respective creditors based on facts and law, with Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin providing cooperation. Article 6 stipulated that other debts of Liyumen Company beyond the above five debts would still be cleared and repaid by Yizhifan Company, with Hou Qingbin and Lizhao Company assuming joint and several guarantee liability.

On November 17, 2015, Yizhifan Company, Zhaobangji Company, Shenzhen Xinnuo Telecom Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinnuo Telecom Company), Hou Qingbin, and Liyumen Company jointly entered into a Supplementary Agreement. The Supplementary Agreement confirmed the performance of the August 26 Agreement, confirming that items (4) and (5) of the above five debts had been fully performed, but item (1) remained pending litigation in the Gao Yingcan case, with the specific amount not yet determined; item (2) had been paid RMB 33 million, but as Jianbang Company had filed a lawsuit with the court, the balance had not yet been paid; item (3) had been paid RMB 40 million, but as Xinnuo Telecom Company issued a notice to Zhaobangji Company on August 11, 2015 to suspend payment, the remaining RMB 40 million had not been paid. The parties agreed: 1. For the RMB 120 million portion for the Gao Yingcan case, the amount would be based on the actual amount incurred upon conclusion of that case. Any excess would be handled according to previous agreements. If the actual amount incurred was less than RMB 120 million, the balance, after deducting costs such as litigation fees and attorney fees, would belong to Xinnuo Telecom Company. 2. For the RMB 50 million for Jianbang Company's debt, RMB 33 million had been paid, and the balance (RMB 17 million) would be paid within five days from the date of signing this agreement. 3. For the remaining balance and handling of the debt arising from loans from Chaoshang Company and its affiliate Wu Yiqun, since RMB 40 million had been paid, the balance remained unpaid due to Xinnuo Telecom Company's suspension notice. Zhaobangji Company should pay this amount only after receiving a payment notice from Xinnuo Telecom Company. However, since Liyumen Company was neither the actual borrower nor the actual user of the loan, the actual borrower or user was Xinnuo Telecom Company. Hou Qingbin, as the actual controller of Xinnuo Telecom Company, could resolve the relevant rights and interests related to the borrowing relationship from Chaoshang Company through litigation, but regardless of the method, the relevant rights and interests of Liyumen Company must not be harmed. Article 4 of the Supplementary Agreement confirmed the account balance of Liyumen Company and other issues.

On November 10, 2014, Zhaobangji Company increased its capital contribution to Liyumen Company by RMB 80 million, resulting in Zhaobangji Company holding 96.67% equity of Liyumen Company and Kangnuofu Company holding 3.33% equity. Subsequently, further changes were made; currently, the equity structure of Liyumen Company was Zhaobangji Company holding 90% equity and Kangnuofu Company holding 10% equity. On April 8, 2015, Kangnuofu Company pledged its 10% equity, and Zhaobangji Company pledged its 90% equity to Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Hongwei Sub-branch, and Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Huaqiaocheng Sub-branch.

On November 19, 2015, a mediation agreement was reached in the case of the loan contract dispute between Jianbang Company, Liyumen Company, Xinnuo Telecom Company, Hou Qingbin, and Zhang Yu at the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, and a civil mediation document was issued by the court. To perform the obligations under the mediation document, Zhang Yu, on the instruction of Zhaobangji Company, transferred RMB 15 million to Jianbang Company on November 27, 2015, and separately transferred RMB 2 million to Xinnuo Telecom Company.

The court of first instance held that, regarding the cause of action in this case. Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on the grounds of a dispute over a pledge right. However, based on the facts found by the court of first instance, no pledge right was established in this case, and the parties did not have any agreement on establishing a pledge right. The claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin primarily concerned the validity of the contracts involved and the legal consequences after determining the validity of those contracts. Therefore, the cause of action in this case should be a contract dispute.

Based on the arguments of the parties, the issues in dispute in this case were: 1. Whether Hou Qingbin is a qualified plaintiff in this case; 2. Whether Liyumen Company is a qualified defendant in this case; 3. How to determine the nature and validity of the August 26 Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement; 4. Whether the conditions for rescission of the April 25 Equity Guarantee Agreement were met.

1. Whether Hou Qingbin is a qualified plaintiff in this case

Kangnuofu Company argued that Hou Qingbin was not a qualified plaintiff in this case. The reason was that Hou Qingbin was neither the pledgee, the pledgor, nor one of the owners of the 30% equity in the contract of fluid quality he alleged. Hou Qingbin's contractual status in the August 26 Agreement, the April 25 Equity Guarantee Agreement, and other agreements was that of a "guarantor," so he had no right to claim rights related to the 30% equity in this case. According to the business registration information, Hou Qingbin was not a shareholder of Yizhifan Company, so he had no right to assert claims in this case, and his lawsuit should be dismissed.

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin's first claim was: to legally declare the August 26 Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement invalid. Based on the facts found by the court of first instance, Hou Qingbin, as a party to the contract, signed the August 26 Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement. The validity of these contracts was legally relevant to him, and he had the right to file corresponding claims regarding the determination of the validity of these contracts, which met the requirements for a plaintiff under Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the court did not support Kangnuofu Company's contention that Hou Qingbin was not a qualified plaintiff in this case.

2. Whether Liyumen Company is a qualified defendant in this case

Liyumen Company argued that it was not a qualified defendant in this case. The reason was that there was neither a contractual relationship nor a tort relationship between Liyumen Company and Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin. Including Liyumen Company as a defendant in this case was a mistake in the lawsuit, and the lawsuit against Liyumen Company by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin should be dismissed.

The court of first instance held that the claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin included: to legally declare the August 26 Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement invalid; and to legally confirm that Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin enjoy 30% of the project rights and interests of Liyumen Company. Based on the facts found by the court of first instance, Liyumen Company signed the August 26 Agreement. In that agreement, Liyumen Company and Zhaobangji Company jointly undertook to resolve the debts originally owed by Yizhifan Company, Hou Qingbin, and others within the total amount of RMB 406 million; Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin also undertook to completely withdraw from Liyumen Company and no longer have any rights in Liyumen Company. Therefore, the August 26 Agreement created corresponding rights and obligations between Liyumen Company and Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin. Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin's claim to declare that agreement invalid was legally relevant to Liyumen Company, making Liyumen Company a qualified defendant in this case. Therefore, the court did not support Liyumen Company's contention that it was not a qualified defendant.

3. How to determine the nature and validity of the August 26 Agreement and the Supplementary Agreement

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin argued that the above agreements were invalid for two main reasons: first, the agreements constituted a contract of fluid quality for security; second, the agreements violated the mandatory liquidation obligations of transfer for guarantee and in fact improperly extracted undue gains. Zhaobangji Company argued that the above agreements were equity transfer agreements, did not involve a contract of fluid quality, and were legally valid.

This disputed issue is the core issue in the trial of this case. According to the opinions of the claims filed by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin, their assertion that the aforementioned agreements are invalid for violating the prohibition on fluid pacts is based on Article 211 of the Real Right Law of the People's Republic of China: "Before the expiration of the debt performance period, the pledgee shall not agree with the pledgor that the pledged property shall vest in the obligee if the obligor fails to perform the due debt." This provision is located in Chapter 17 "Pledge Right" of the Real Right Law of the People's Republic of China, and therefore its application is premised on the establishment of a pledge right. However, based on the facts found in this case, the disputed 30% equity interest was not registered as a pledge in accordance with Article 224 of the Real Right Law of the People's Republic of China to establish a right of pledge, nor did the August 26 Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement contain any agreement on the establishment of a pledge. Therefore, the legal relationship involved in the aforementioned agreements does not fall within the scope directly regulated by Article 211 of the Real Right Law of the People's Republic of China. The legislative purpose of prohibiting fluid pacts is that debtors are often compelled by financial difficulties to provide high-value pledged property to secure a relatively small claim; the creditor may take advantage of the debtor's distress to force the debtor to enter into a fluid pact, so that when the debtor fails to repay the debt, the creditor automatically acquires ownership of the pledged property, reaping excessive profits and undermining the civil law principles of fairness and exchange of equal value. Therefore, although this case does not fall within the scope directly regulated by Article 211 of the Real Right Law of the People's Republic of China, it should equally comply with the basic civil law principles of fairness and exchange of equal value reflected in that legal provision.

Security transfer refers to an atypical security interest in property where the debtor or a third party transfers the ownership and other rights of the security object to the security holder to secure the debtor's debt, so that the security holder, within the scope not exceeding the purpose of security, shall return the security object to the debtor or third party upon repayment of the debt, and if the debt is not performed, the security holder may receive priority compensation from the object. The Real Right Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws do not expressly provide for the system of security transfer, but they do not prohibit parties from entering into security transfer contracts based on the principle of freedom of contract, and the legal relationship of security transfer is regulated by the rules of contract law. In judicial practice, security transfer contracts may appear in various forms such as sales contracts or equity transfer contracts. When dealing with such contracts that exhibit the characteristics of security transfer, the court shall respect the true expression of intent of the parties and examine whether the true purpose of the parties in entering into such contracts is to provide security for the performance of other contracts or to acquire ownership of the subject matter by paying consideration. At the same time, to avoid the security transfer creditor using their advantageous negotiating position to reap excessive profits and undermine the civil law principles of fairness and exchange of equal value, when the secured claim cannot be realized, the security transfer creditor cannot automatically acquire ownership of the subject matter; the means of realizing their rights and interests is to receive compensation from the value of the subject matter.

From the facts found by this court, it can be known that the cooperation between Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company, Ltd. regarding the Liyumen Company and the target project began with the April 2 Project Cooperation Agreement. As the cooperation progressed, the rights and obligations of the parties were further adjusted and detailed by the April 25 Equity Security Agreement. Therefore, to determine the nature and validity of the August 26 Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement, it is necessary to systematically examine the relevant contents of the above four agreements.

In the April 2 Project Cooperation Agreement, Yizhifan Company and others undertook to handle and bear responsibility for the Heijian litigation, ensuring that within twenty days after the 70% equity in Liyumen Company was registered in the name of Zhaobangji Company, the preservation seizure placed on the target project land would be removed by means such as replacement. Yizhifan Company undertook to use its 30% equity in Liyumen Company and the corresponding undistributed rights and interests as security for the performance of the above obligation. If Yizhifan Company and others failed to remove the seizure placed on the target project land within one month after the signing of this agreement, Zhaobangji Company had the right to negotiate with the relevant court or settle with the opposing party in the lawsuit in its own name or in the name of the project company, in order to promptly lift the seizure placed on the target project land. The relevant costs and expenses incurred therefrom were to be repaid by Yizhifan Company and others to Zhaobangji Company on a joint and several liability basis, or offset against Zhaobangji Company with Yizhifan Company's equity in Liyumen Company and the corresponding undistributed rights and interests. However, when paying the above costs or expenses, Zhaobangji Company should negotiate with Yizhifan Company to determine them. From the above provisions of the April 2 Project Cooperation Agreement, it can be seen that when the agreed conditions are fulfilled, Yizhifan Company could choose to pay the relevant costs or expenses to Zhaobangji Company, or choose to offset with the disputed 30% equity. At that time, the value of the disputed 30% equity, the method of offset, etc., were not yet determined and still required further negotiation between Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company.

In the April 25 Equity Security Agreement, Yizhifan Company expressly agreed to provide the disputed 30% equity as security to Zhaobangji Company to ensure that Yizhifan Company could pay and repay the relevant debts of Liyumen Company, costs of relevant litigation, later principal and interest of borrowings from Zhaobangji Company, later bank loan principal and interest of Liyumen Company to be borne by Yizhifan Company, later development and construction funds of the target project to be borne by Yizhifan Company, etc. Compared with the provisions of the April 2 Project Cooperation Agreement, the April 25 Equity Security Agreement increased and clarified the content secured by the disputed 30% equity, and specified that the method of security was to transfer the disputed 30% equity to Kangnuofu Company, which was jointly held by Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company. At the same time, the agreement specified that Yizhifan Company was still the actual owner of the disputed 30% equity, the shareholder rights and obligations were exercised by Yizhifan Company, and without the consent of both Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company, neither party could dispose of the disputed 30% equity. After the settlement conditions agreed in the agreement were met, Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company would conduct a final settlement of Yizhifan Company's various repayment and payment obligations. If Yizhifan Company fully performed various repayment and payment obligations, Zhaobangji Company should ensure that the disputed 30% equity was returned to Yizhifan Company. If Yizhifan Company failed to settle various repayment and payment obligations, or if Zhaobangji Company had repaid and paid on behalf of Yizhifan Company, Zhaobangji Company had the right to demand Yizhifan Company to repay or offset with the rights and interests corresponding to the disputed 30% equity. The parties also agreed on a method of offset based on market value appraisal. Therefore, this method of security can be understood as Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company jointly managing the disputed 30% equity. Although Yizhifan Company transferred the disputed 30% equity to Kangnuofu Company, its true intention was not to abandon ownership of the disputed 30% equity. When the agreed conditions were met, Yizhifan Company could still retrieve the disputed 30% equity. Therefore, the April 25 Equity Security Agreement embodied the characteristics of security transfer, and for the case where Yizhifan Company could not perform its debts, the agreement provided for a method of offset based on market value appraisal with respect to the disputed 30% equity, rather than Zhaobangji Company or Kangnuofu Company automatically acquiring ownership of the disputed 30% equity, which complied with the principles of fairness and exchange of equal value.

In the August 26 Agreement, the parties confirmed the debts that Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin had failed to clear and repay, and clarified that, after a market appraisal of the entire project, the rights and interests enjoyed by Yizhifan Company in the project company were insufficient to repay the above debts. The parties agreed that the debts owed by Yizhifan Company, Hou Qingbin, and Lizhao Company would be resolved by Zhaobangji Company and Liyumen Company within the scope of RMB 406 million, and at the same time, Yizhifan Company abandoned the disputed 30% equity, which would vest in Zhaobangji Company. The Supplemental Agreement confirmed the fact that Zhaobangji Company had performed its obligations in accordance with the plan for the use of the RMB 406 million as agreed in the August 26 Agreement. At this point, the security transfer relationship set up in the April 25 Equity Security Agreement between Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company with respect to the disputed 30% equity had been terminated by the August 26 Agreement. Yizhifan Company expressly abandoned ownership of the disputed 30% equity and no longer retained the right provided in the April 25 Equity Security Agreement to retrieve the disputed 30% equity upon satisfaction of certain conditions. Therefore, the nature of the August 26 Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement should be determined as equity transfer agreements, and the true expression of intent of Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company under these agreements was to transfer ownership of the disputed 30% equity.

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin asserted that when the agreement was signed, the principal secured obligation had not yet become due, nor had the liquidation period for the security property arrived; the security property was obtained without liquidation before the performance period expired, violating the mandatory liquidation obligation in security transfer, and Zhaobangji Company in fact grabbed improper benefits; therefore, the agreement was an invalid contract. The court does not adopt the above assertions of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin. The reasons are as follows: (1) The August 26 Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement confirm that under the circumstance that Yizhifan Company failed to clear and repay the relevant five debts, Zhaobangji Company did not automatically acquire the disputed 30% equity, but rather acquired it by paying RMB 406 million to resolve the relevant five debts as consideration. (2) Although, as Yizhifan Company asserts, some of the five debts were not yet due and some were still in litigation with the final amount not determined, none of the creditors of these five debts was Zhaobangji Company. What was undetermined was only the amount of debt between Yizhifan Company and the creditors of these five debts. Zhaobangji Company's obligation to pay the consideration of RMB 406 million was fixed and would not change due to fluctuations in the amount of the five debts. According to the record of the Supplemental Agreement, Zhaobangji Company had already repaid two of the five debts, namely: the principal and interest of the Guangzhou Bank loan of RMB 100 million to be borne by Yizhifan Company, and the principal and interest of the loan of RMB 50 million from Xu Weishan totaling RMB 56 million. For the remaining three debts, the Supplemental Agreement also provided for the treatment if the actual debts were less or more than the agreed amounts. For example, for the RMB 120 million part used for the Gao Yingcan case, any excess amount would be repaid by Yizhifan Company, with Hou Qingbin and Lizhao Company bearing joint and several suretyship liability; if the actual amount incurred was less than RMB 120 million, the balance, after deducting costs such as litigation fees and attorney fees, would belong to Xinnuo Telecom Company. For the debt of RMB 50 million to Jianbang Company, Zhaobangji Company had already paid RMB 33 million, and later, to perform the contents of the mediation letter, on November 27, 2015, it commissioned Zhang Yu to transfer RMB 15 million to Jianbang Company by bank transfer, and also separately transferred RMB 2 million to Xinnuo Telecom Company by bank transfer. For the RMB 80 million used to settle the remaining balance of borrowings from Chaosheng Company and its related person Wu Yiqun and to handle the matter, Zhaobangji Company had already paid RMB 40 million, and the balance was not paid due to a notice from Xinnuo Telecom Company suspending payment; this amount would be paid by Zhaobangji Company upon receipt of a payment notice from Xinnuo Telecom Company. Therefore, even if, after Yizhifan Company settled the relevant debts with the creditors of the five debts, the amount of debt turned out to be less than RMB 406 million, Zhaobangji Company would not thereby obtain improper benefits. (3) The April 25 Equity Security Agreement provided that the final settlement period for Yizhifan Company's various repayment and payment obligations would be when the Liyumen Company was fully completed and accepted, had obtained initial registration, and was ready for separate property right registration. However, laws and regulations do not prohibit Yizhifan Company, when it foresees that it cannot perform its contractual obligations as agreed, from settling early with Zhaobangji Company and transferring the disputed 30% equity at a fixed price to avoid its external debt repayment obligations. Yizhifan Company, as the owner of the disputed 30% equity, should have a clear understanding of the value of that equity. As a highly rational commercial actor, it also has a duty of prudence in making commercial judgments. The Company Law of the People's Republic of China does not make appraisal or auction of company assets and equity value a mandatory procedure for equity transfer, nor does it impose mandatory provisions on whether the equity transfer price must match its actual value. The amount of RMB 406 million was the result of joint agreement among the parties to the agreement, reflecting the principle of party autonomy of the parties to the agreement. Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin have not submitted evidence to prove that the signing of the disputed agreements violated the principle of party autonomy. In summary, the court of first instance held that the August 26 Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement do not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, nor do they violate the civil law principles of fairness and exchange of equal value. They are lawful and valid, and the parties shall perform them as agreed. The commitments made by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin in the above agreements to abandon the disputed 30% equity, to have no rights in Liyumen Company, and to have no rights in the target project are valid. The claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin that the August 26 Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement are invalid, and the request to confirm that Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin enjoy 30% of the project rights and interests of Liyumen Company, lack factual and legal basis, and this court does not support them.

IV. Whether the disputed April 25 Equity Security Agreement meets the conditions for rescission

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin assert that Zhaobangji Company failed to provide the financing loan of RMB 250 million to Yizhifan Company as agreed, and that Kangnuofu Company and Zhaobangji Company transferred the disputed 30% equity without permission from Yizhifan Company, constituting a breach of contract that frustrated the purpose of the contract. Therefore, the disputed April 25 Equity Security Agreement should be rescinded, and Zhaobangji Company and Kangnuofu Company should return the disputed 30% equity to Yizhifan Company.

Regarding the above assertions of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin, this court analyzes and determines as follows: 1. Regarding the issue that Zhaobangji Company failed to provide the financing loan of RMB 250 million to Yizhifan Company as agreed. Section 2.3 of the April 25 Equity Security Agreement stipulates: After the signing of this agreement, if Yizhifan Company needs to obtain a financing loan from Zhaobangji Company, Yizhifan Company shall transfer the 49% equity held by Luo Xiaotang in Kangnuofu Company to Zhaobangji Company or a company (or individual) designated by Zhaobangji Company, to serve as security for the financing loan. Upon examination of the facts of this case, Yizhifan Company did not transfer the 49% equity held by Luo Xiaotang in Kangnuofu Company to Zhaobangji Company or a company (or individual) designated by Zhaobangji Company. Therefore, the prerequisite for Yizhifan Company to obtain a financing loan from Zhaobangji Company was not satisfied, and Zhaobangji Company's failure to provide the financing loan to Yizhifan Company does not constitute a ground for Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin to exercise the right to rescind the contract. 2. Regarding the issue that Kangnuofu Company and Zhaobangji Company transferred the disputed 30% equity. According to the facts found in this case, the acts of Kangnuofu Company and Zhaobangji Company in disposing of the equity in Liyumen Company all occurred after the August 26 Agreement came into effect. As discussed above, the August 26 Agreement is an equity transfer agreement whereby Yizhifan Company transferred the disputed 30% equity to Zhaobangji Company. The parties had mutually agreed to terminate the security transfer legal relationship established by the April 25 Equity Security Agreement and established an equity transfer contractual relationship. After the August 26 Agreement came into effect, Yizhifan Company had abandoned ownership of the disputed 30% equity. The acts of Zhaobangji Company and Kangnuofu Company in disposing of the equity in Liyumen Company do not constitute a breach of contract. In summary, the claim of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin to rescind the April 25 Equity Security Agreement and the assertion that Zhaobangji Company and Kangnuofu Company should return the disputed 30% equity to Yizhifan Company lack factual and legal basis and are not supported.

In conclusion, the claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin are not established, and the court of first instance did not support them. In accordance with Article 8 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: All claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin are dismissed. The case acceptance fee is RMB 3,567,017, and the property preservation fee is RMB 5,000, to be borne by Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin.

The facts found by this court on second-instance trial are consistent with the facts found by the court of first instance.

Additionally, it is found that Section 4.2 of the April 25 Equity Security Agreement stipulates: "During the construction period of the target project, Party A (Yizhifan Company) and Party B (Zhaobangji Company) shall, each year from the date of signing this agreement, entrust a professional institution to appraise the market value of the target project and the rights and interests corresponding to Party A (excluding taxes and fees). If the appraisal result shows that the rights and interests enjoyed by Party A in the target project... are insufficient to satisfy the repayment and payment obligations agreed in Article 1 of this agreement... then Party A and Party B shall negotiate and take the following measures: Party A shall immediately discharge the debt to reduce it, or Party A shall make additional investment to increase the equity share, or Party A shall transfer its equity in the project company to Party B, and Party B shall discharge the corresponding amount of debt on behalf of Party A."

This court is of the opinion that, based on the parties' claims and defenses, the issues in dispute in this second-instance trial are: 1. How should the nature and validity of the disputed August 26 Agreement be determined. 2. Whether the disputed April 25 Equity Security Agreement meets the conditions for rescission.

I. Regarding the issue of how the nature and validity of the disputed August 26 Agreement should be determined.

8.26 Agreement is an agreement signed by the parties in the course of the transaction involved in this case. To determine the nature of this Agreement, it is necessary to systematically review the entire transaction arrangement, i.e., the contents of the four agreements signed successively. The 4.2 Project Cooperation Agreement mainly involves Yizhifan Company transferring its 70% equity in Liyumen Company to Zhaobangji Company. While disclosing the debts of Liyumen Company, Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin explicitly undertook to handle and assume responsibility for the Heijian lawsuit, and Yizhifan Company also pledged its remaining 30% equity in Liyumen Company and the corresponding undistributed rights and interests as security for the performance of the above debts. The above provisions did not involve the transfer of the 30% equity or guarantee by transfer. The 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement states at the outset that to ensure Yizhifan Company can assume the obligations of debt repayment and subsequent fund payment, the company is willing to transfer its 30% equity in Liyumen Company by way of transfer of title as a pledge to Kangnuofu Company, a company jointly held by Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company. This agreement includes within the scope of security the debts of Yizhifan Company and Liyumen Company to external creditors, as well as Yizhifan Company's contingent borrowing debt of RMB 250 million to Zhaobangji Company. Considering that the purpose of Yizhifan Company transferring the 30% equity to Kangnuofu Company was not to transfer the equity, but to secure the performance of relevant debts, i.e., if Yizhifan Company fully performs its repayment and payment obligations, it may request the return of the 30% equity; if it fails to perform or Zhaobangji Company pays on its behalf, Zhaobangji Company may use the rights and interests corresponding to the 30% equity to offset, it can be determined that the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement is essentially an agreement establishing a guarantee by transfer. The first-instance judgment's finding that this agreement reflects the characteristics of a guarantee by transfer is not improper. The 8.26 Agreement, in its preamble "Whereas" section, briefly states the signing and main contents of the 4.2 Project Cooperation Agreement and the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement, and then clearly states that due to reasons attributable to Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin, three debts have not been cleared and repaid as agreed, two disclosed debts have not yet matured, and after a market evaluation of the entire project, all parties acknowledge that the rights and interests held by Yizhifan Company in Liyumen Company are insufficient to repay the above debts. In view of this, this Agreement provides that Yizhifan Company abandons the 30% equity already transferred to Kangnuofu Company, which shall belong to Zhaobangji Company, and at the same time, the above five debts shall be resolved by Zhaobangji Company and Liyumen Company within the total amount of RMB 406 million. The subsequent Supplemental Agreement further confirmed the specific circumstances of Zhaobangji Company's performance of the above five debts within RMB 406 million as agreed in the 8.26 Agreement. It can be seen that the 8.26 Agreement succeeds the two previous agreements. Although it does not involve the security of the 30% equity, i.e., Yizhifan Company no longer retains the right to retrieve the 30% equity under certain conditions as set in the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement, this agreement was made on the basis of the guarantee by transfer right established by the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement, setting out how Zhaobangji Company, as the holder of the guarantee by transfer right, may specifically realize that right. The first-instance judgment improperly severed the relationship between the above agreements, finding that the 30% equity had been converted from the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer to consideration of RMB 406 million, and that the guarantee by transfer relationship established by the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement had been terminated by the 8.26 Agreement, thereby determining that the 8.26 Agreement was an equity transfer agreement. This is indeed improper, and this court hereby corrects it. The claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin that the 8.26 Agreement and the four agreements before and after actually constitute a series of overall agreements on the guarantee by transfer of the 30% equity are established and are adopted by this court.

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin claim that the 8.26 Agreement has the nature of a guarantee by transfer, and argue that it is invalid on the grounds that at the time of signing, some debts had not yet fallen due, the 30% equity involved was not evaluated and liquidated as agreed, and Zhaobangji Company, by taking advantage of its dominant position as a creditor, forced Yizhifan Company to abandon the 30% equity to offset external liabilities of RMB 406 million. This court finds that the claims of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin also cannot be sustained, for the following specific reasons:

First, regarding the issue that some debts had not yet fallen due. In this case, Yizhifan Company fulfilled relevant debts, including the above five debts, to external monetary creditors as its contractual obligation to Zhaobangji Company. For the performance of this contractual obligation, a guarantee by transfer relationship was established between Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company, not between Yizhifan Company and the external monetary creditors. The so-called "some debts not yet due" refers to two loan debts of Yizhifan Company and others to external parties that had not yet matured. A guarantee by transfer is usually established by signing an agreement and transferring ownership or other rights in the subject matter before the debt performance period expires; otherwise, it would not constitute a method of security but merely a way of performing the debt. The parties in this case signed the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement when some debts were not yet due and registered the transfer to establish a guarantee by transfer right, which satisfies the above requirement. The establishment of a guarantee by transfer should occur before the debt performance period expires. However, regarding the realization of the guarantee by transfer, reference should be made to Article 170 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, which requires that the conditions for realization, such as the debtor's failure to perform a due debt or the occurrence of an event agreed by the parties, be satisfied. The 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement stipulates that the final settlement period for all repayment and payment obligations of Yizhifan Company shall be when the target project is fully completed, accepted, and registered, and is ready for separate property rights registration; however, during the construction period, if an evaluation shows that Yizhifan Company's 30% interest in the target project is insufficient to repay the relevant debts and fulfill payment obligations, Yizhifan Company shall transfer its equity to Zhaobangji Company, and the latter shall repay the corresponding amount of debts on its behalf. It can be seen that, according to the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement, the circumstance where the rights and interests corresponding to Yizhifan Company's 30% equity are insufficient to repay the relevant debts becomes the agreed condition for Zhaobangji Company to exercise the guarantee by transfer right. In fact, it was precisely when this agreed condition was met that the parties signed the 8.26 Agreement to specifically realize the guarantee by transfer right involved. Therefore, the fact that two loan debts of Yizhifan Company and others to external parties were not yet due does not affect the validity of the 8.26 Agreement, which specifically realizes the guarantee by transfer right between Yizhifan Company and Zhaobangji Company.

Second, regarding the liquidation issue in realizing the guarantee by transfer. In the establishment of a guarantee by transfer, ownership of the subject matter is usually transferred to the creditor. To protect the debtor's interests and prevent situations similar to forfeiture clauses where the creditor obtains a difference between the appraised value of the subject matter and the amount of the claim, the realization of the guarantee by transfer right should impose a liquidation obligation on the parties. In this case, the parties also clearly stipulated a liquidation clause in the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement, i.e., if after settlement Yizhifan Company fully performs its repayment and payment obligations, Yizhifan Company may request the return of the 30% equity; if it fails to perform or Zhaobangji Company pays on its behalf, Zhaobangji Company may require offsetting using the rights and interests corresponding to Yizhifan Company's 30% equity in Liyumen Company (i.e., the real estate property apportionable according to the equity ratio), with the specific offset method being 90% of the market sales price as appraised. Liquidation requires a comparison between the appraised value of the subject matter and the amount of the claim, which typically involves determining the appraised value of the subject matter but may also involve determining the amount of the claim. First, regarding the determination of the value of the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer. Although the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement required a professional appraisal agency's evaluation, according to the subsequently signed 8.26 Agreement, the parties clearly changed the original agreement and reached a consensus on the value of the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer at RMB 406 million. This amount of RMB 406 million was the result of negotiation among all parties to the agreement, reflecting the autonomy of the parties. Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin did not submit evidence proving that the signing of the agreement involved circumstances violating the principle of autonomy. Therefore, it is not improper in this case to determine the value of the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer as RMB 406 million, the amount agreed upon by all parties. Second, regarding the determination of the amount of the claim. The 8.26 Agreement clearly states that Zhaobangji Company and others are required to resolve the aforementioned five debts within the total amount of RMB 406 million, and allocates specific amounts for these five debts totaling RMB 406 million. Accordingly, it can be determined that the value of the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer and the total amount of debts have been preliminarily determined and are equal. However, considering that the amount of Yizhifan Company's debts to external parties may change, the parties further agreed on a liquidation obligation based on settling the debt amount according to the facts. For example, the 8.26 Agreement stipulates that Zhaobangji Company and Liyumen Company shall settle with each creditor according to the facts; the Supplemental Agreement more clearly provides that the portion of RMB 120 million for the Gao Yingcan case shall be based on the actual amount incurred at the conclusion of that case, and any balance remaining after the actual repayment to creditors falls short of the original debt amount shall belong to Xinnuo Telecom Company (an affiliate of Yizhifan Company) actually controlled by Hou Qingbin. In fact, for the RMB 50 million debt of Jianbang Company, after Zhaobangji Company paid RMB 48 million to Jianbang Company to settle that debt, the relevant external party also paid the balance of RMB 2 million to Xinnuo Telecom Company as entrusted by Zhaobangji Company. It can be seen that in this case, the value of the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer has been determined by the parties' agreement. However, because the amount of the debt may change, the liquidation obligation of the parties is mainly reflected in returning the difference between the debt amount and the value of the subject matter to the obligor of the guarantee by transfer, i.e., Yizhifan Company, based on the final settled debt amount according to the facts. The parties not only agreed to but also actually performed the liquidation obligation. Therefore, this court does not support Yizhifan Company's claim that the guarantee by transfer was not liquidated.

II. Whether the 4.25 Equity Pledge Agreement involved meets the conditions for rescission

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin claim that they have a contractual right of rescission on the ground that Kangnuofu Company and Zhaobangji Company pledged the 30% equity involved without the consent of Yizhifan Company. As stated above, there is no ground for invalidity of the 8.26 Agreement. According to the facts found in the first-instance judgment, the acts of Kangnuofu Company and Zhaobangji Company in pledging the equity of Liyumen Company occurred after the 8.26 Agreement took effect. Moreover, after the Agreement took effect, Zhaobangji Company had already realized the guarantee by transfer right previously agreed upon, and Yizhifan Company no longer had any rights to the subject matter of the guarantee by transfer, i.e., the 30% equity. Therefore, the pledge of Liyumen Company's equity by Zhaobangji Company and Kangnuofu Company did not constitute a breach of contract. Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin also do not have a contractual right of rescission for this reason.

Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin claim that the 8.26 Agreement illegally disposed of the 30% equity, making it impossible to achieve the contractual purpose of Yizhifan Company's ownership of the 30% equity, and that Liyumen Company's mortgage of the land use rights and the project under construction, which are its core assets, to external parties severely damaged Yizhifan Company's 30% project interest, making it impossible to achieve the contractual purpose of liquidating the 30% equity. Therefore, Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin have a statutory right of rescission. As discussed above, the 8.26 Agreement does not involve the illegal disposal of the 30% equity, and the failure to achieve the contractual purpose of Yizhifan Company's ownership of the 30% equity was not caused by Zhaobangji Company. Liyumen Company's mortgage of its core assets, i.e., the land use rights and the project under construction, to external parties is a matter within the normal scope of the company's business operations and is unrelated to Yizhifan Company's claim of damage to its 30% project interest. Therefore, the claim of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin that they have a statutory right of rescission cannot be sustained.

In summary, the facts found in the first-instance judgment are clear. Although there is a defect in the application of law, i.e., an improper characterization of the nature of the contract, the result of the judgment is correct and should be affirmed. The appeals of Yizhifan Company and Hou Qingbin are not established and are not supported by this court. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 334 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 3,567,017 shall be borne by Shenzhen Yizhifan Trade Co., Ltd. and Hou Qingbin.

This judgment is final.
